startup.name: Rivet
startup.one_liner: Explore dozens of design directions with your agent
startup.description: Rivet helps designers explore dozens of design directions from their coding agent. The input gives no team size and only a short description; the pitch is a design exploration layer between agents and designers. San Francisco, Fall 2025 batch.

yc_acceptance.basis: Start from the third party prior of about 1 percent (references/yc_acceptance.md). Description is one sentence, team size is unknown and no traction is stated, so no upward adjustment. AI design tools are a hot topic that matches current YC interest but the space is crowded, so about 1 percent.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because the pitch is thin and sits in a crowded set of AI design tools, from prototyping products to canvas tools for agents. Without an obvious paying buyer or traction, reviewers see a feature that Figma or the coding agent vendors can ship.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --calibration-only --tag AI gave seed lower/known/upper 51%/64%/71%, cond 64% (n=183), ever and not windowed. Window cut: calibration median 7 months, p75 19.5 months.
anchors.adjustment_reason: About 0.66 times the 0.64 ever anchor because the window is 13 months and takeover risk is 5, with a named analog (visly) that ended in a small acquisition; no lift for sector heat.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round under $3M from angels and a small fund, the most common path for a 2 or 3 person team without revenue. Window is 13 months from 2025-10-06 to 2026-11-17.
Institutional seed of $3M to $6M, the middle of the 2022 and later table (median about $3.5M to $4M).
Larger institutional seed of $6M to $12M, which the 2026 winners test showed is more common than forecasts assumed.
Hot round above $12M, possible only if the product shows fast usage; upside band.

ladder.why_it_fails: Investors will likely pass because exploration of design directions looks like a feature that agent vendors and Figma will ship. Variant and polymet show AI design companies stay small without a paying wedge, and the one sentence pitch shows no traction. A seed needs fast usage by working designers.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --calibration-only --tag AI gave series_a 15%/19%/36%, cond 30% (n=117). Median 28 months.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Given a seed, a Series A within 13 months of the batch is early (calibration p25 is 19 months) and no payer is proven, so about a quarter of the ever anchor.

bands.rationale: Thin Series A or extended seed below the 2022 and later p25 of $11M, typical when growth is slower than hoped.
Typical Series A near the 2022 and later median of about $14M to $15M.
Strong Series A of $16M to $30M when revenue growth is clear and a lead investor competes, above the 2022 and later p75 of about $20M.
Breakout Series A above $30M, possible only for a category leader with fast revenue growth; upside band.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series A needs recurring revenue from design teams. Rivet would need to prove designers pay for exploration rather than using a free agent. Noya software and variant did not reach large rounds early, so it likely misses the revenue bar that investors set for design tooling, where free agent features compete.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --calibration-only --tag AI gave series_b 5%/6%/26%, cond 31% (n=35). Ever.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Below the 0.31 anchor because of copy risk.

bands.rationale: Down or flat round, below the 2022 and later p25 of $27M.
Typical Series B near the $32M to $40M median.
Upside band at the p75 of $55M and above.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series B requires a platform with real scale. Design tooling is dominated by Figma, and an exploration layer that does not own the file format cannot grow past a small base of individual designers who churn quickly, which investors at that stage will not fund.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --calibration-only --tag AI gave series_c 2%/3%/23%, cond 45% (n=11). Ever.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Below 0.45 anchor since few design tools reach growth rounds.

bands.rationale: Smaller growth round or bridge financing below the 2022 and later series C p25 of about $50M.
Typical Series C near the $60M to $74M median.
Upside band for a category leader, above the 2022 and later series C p75 of about $100M.

ladder.why_it_fails: Growth rounds would require displacing or integrating with Figma at scale. Few design tool startups reach that stage, and visly ended in an acquisition well before it. Rivet would more likely be acquired by an agent or design vendor than raise a growth round.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The usual end is a stall: design tooling for agents is a feature of the coding agent or of Figma, and designers rarely pay for a separate exploration step. Analogs such as noya software and visly show that design tool startups face a strong incumbent and slow monetization.

analogs.outcome_summary: Active at small scale; no institutional round found early on.

analogs.relevance: Product design tool for non designers, Winter 2023.

analogs.outcome_summary: Early stage with no major round recorded.

analogs.relevance: Visual builder of React components, Winter 2019.

analogs.outcome_summary: Survived on a narrow wedge, modest funding.

killers.risk: Figma, Cursor and coding agent vendors add multi direction exploration natively
killers.evidence: AI prototyping from Figma and agent vendors was shipping through 2025; visly ended in acquisition, not independence.
killers.mitigation: Be the neutral layer that works across agents and saves designer time on measurable tasks.

killers.risk: No clear payer: designers use free exploration and engineers decide the stack
killers.evidence: Design tool startups struggle to monetize, as variant and polymet show early.
killers.mitigation: Sell to design teams at product companies with a per seat price tied to shipped work.

killers.risk: Thin team and unclear differentiation at demo day
killers.evidence: The description gives a single sentence and no team size.
killers.mitigation: Publish concrete exploration quality results against baseline prompting.

technical_complexity.rationale: A layer that drives agents to produce many design variants and compares them can be built in weeks by a small team using existing model APIs. Quality, taste and workflow integration are the hard parts, not the engineering.

takeover_risk.rationale: Any coding agent or design tool vendor can add multiple directions to its own product in a few months, and the idea relies on those agents as a platform.

evidence.claim: AI design tools raise seed rounds, showing investor interest
A design tools market report projects continued growth, though paid demand for exploration alone is unproven

actions: Ship a plugin for the main coding agents

actions: Interview teams about what they would pay for

roadmap.goal: Expand from exploration to a workflow

pros.point: Low build cost lets a small team iterate fast
pros.evidence: The product layers on existing agents and model APIs.

brand.name: Rivet
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Rivet" --era 2022+ : invented_or_proper, 5 chars, 2 syllables, no descriptor words.
weaknesses: Rivet is also an existing product name in other categories
brand.rationale: A short concrete noun in the style of Stripe or Figma that is easy to recall, but it does not signal design. Past YC brands such as Replicate and Depot show short nouns work when the product has pull.

narrative.headline: A thin, crowded and easily copied wedge; a seed is possible on AI design heat but the odds are below the cohort anchor.
narrative.general_summary: Rivet pitches design exploration through coding agents. The market has active funded players and investor interest in AI design, but the description is one sentence, team size is unknown and the product depends on agents that platforms can absorb in months. A seed above $1M inside 13 months is plausible given AI heat, yet below the cohort anchor because of copy risk and no stated traction. The odds do not rank Rivet against other companies. Later rounds need a paying design team base, which has not been shown.

assumptions: Information limited to the input file and searches dated before 2025-10-06.
Team size is blank in the input; assumed 2 founders.
Seed means above about $1M from outside investors, excluding the YC deal.
